summary:
Across Australia, the focus remains on community resilience and environmental stewardship. In Central Victoria, fuller water storages at Lake Eppalock and Tullaroop Reservoir are ensuring reliable supply for regional communities, while Ballarat prepares for over $6 million in road maintenance following a wet winter. In Gippsland, significant environmental surveys are underway in Bass Strait to support the proposed 'Star of the South' offshore wind farm, with data being shared with CSIRO and Deakin University to protect marine life. These efforts highlight a constructive approach to balancing energy transition with ecological care.

Internationally, scientific breakthroughs are offering new hope in health and understanding of our planet. Researchers have demonstrated for the first time that human heart muscle can regrow after a heart attack, overturning previous assumptions about cardiac damage. Additionally, a study of an 117-year-old revealed that extreme longevity involves both intense aging and powerful biological protection. In the realm of exploration, a well-preserved feather found in fossilized dinosaur faeces is helping explain how ancestors of modern birds survived mass extinction events.

The human spirit is also on display in global crisis response. In the Philippines, authorities continue searching for 80 missing persons in Coron, emphasizing the determination of rescue teams. In Nepal, the search for survivors in hydropower tunnels continues two weeks after deadly floods, showcasing the persistence of local communities. Meanwhile, in the US, the community of Northfield has demonstrated strong solidarity and cohesion in the face of uncertainty, proving that collective action can provide stability and hope.
